channel.title: Hastings Daily: Council
channel.description: Local news for Hastings, St Leonards, Rye, Bexhill and Battle, three times a day.

item.title: Bexhill community hub to get more than £500,000 in developer funding
item.description: More than £500,000 has been allocated to create a new community hub in Bexhill town centre, Rother District Council said.

item.title: Health watchdog orders rapid improvements at Conquest Hospital emergency care
item.description: The Care Quality Commission has downgraded the urgent and emergency care service at the Conquest Hospital in St Leonards from 'good' to 'requires improvement' and ordered East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust to submit an action plan showing what action it is taking to make immediate improvements. The hospital's overall rating has moved from 'outstanding' to 'good'.

item.title: Rother council to invest £1.3m in seven local projects
item.description: Rother District Council has approved £1.3m from its Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) fund to support seven projects across the district, aimed at improving local facilities, enhancing accessibility and promoting sustainability.

item.title: Hastings council rejects community asset bid for St Leonards convent site
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has turned down a bid to list the former Convent of the Holy Child Jesus on Magdalen Road, St Leonards, as an Asset of Community Value.

item.title: New wheelchair and mobility scooter support group launched in Hastings
item.description: A new support group for residents who use wheelchairs or mobility scooters is being launched in Hastings.

item.title: Saxon Mount School submits plans to replace mobile classrooms with two-storey building
item.description: Saxon Mount School, in Edinburgh Road, St Leonards, has submitted a planning application to replace its four single-storey mobile classrooms with a new two-storey building.

item.title: Update: Rother to consult on 2027/28 budget with £2.72m in reserves
item.description: Rother District Council has launched its public consultation on the draft 2027/28 revenue budget, which runs until 5pm on Wednesday 16 December 2026. The authority said it faces a funding gap of £1.2 million while planning to spend £38m on services, and council leader Doug Oliver urged residents, businesses and community groups to have their say.

item.title: Hastings council budgets £1,937,861 for St Mary in the Castle in 2026/27
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has budgeted spending of £1,937,861 on the Grade II* listed seafront building St Mary in the Castle in the 2026/27 financial year, with the majority set to come forward as capital spending.

item.title: Update: Rother to consult on 2027/28 budget with £2.72m in reserves
item.description: Rother District Council has launched its public consultation on the draft 2027/28 revenue budget, which runs until 5pm on Wednesday 16 December 2026. The authority said it faces a funding gap of £1.2 million while planning to spend £38m on services, and council leader Doug Oliver urged residents, businesses and community groups to have their say.

item.title: Residents to have say on East Sussex supported housing strategy
item.description: People in supported housing across the district can have their say on how it should improve, Rother District Council has said.

item.title: Plans for 42 new homes by St Leonards' Bannatyne's Spa Hotel
item.description: Outline permission has been submitted to build up to 42 homes on land at Bannatyne's Spa Hotel in Hastings Road, St Leonards, according to the latest Hastings Borough Council planning applications.

item.title: Cabinet to consider £1.5m playground funding on Monday
item.description: More than £1.5m to improve playgrounds across the town is set to be considered at the council's Cabinet meeting on Monday evening.

item.title: Call for interest in future use of Sandhurst Recreation Ground
item.description: Hastings Borough Council is asking sports clubs, groups and organisations to register their interest in the future of Sandhurst Recreation Ground. The council wants to know how much demand there is for the sports pitches, which organisations would like to use the site, and whether it could be managed or developed by the community.

item.title: Have your say on renewal of five gated paths in Hastings and St Leonards
item.description: Hastings Borough Council is asking for views on plans to renew gating orders for five public rights of way in Hastings and St Leonards.

item.title: Update: White Rock Gardens could get covered padel and tennis courts
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has announced it is in line to receive £1.3million of investment funding to construct a new covered tennis and padel centre, with a projected overall cost of £1.8million and the council pledging £500,000 match funding.

item.title: West Hill Lift closed for urgent surveys and repairs
item.description: The West Hill Lift has been closed for essential surveys and repairs, according to the Hastings Independent Press.

item.title: Hastings Draft Local Plan: Convent site open for comment until 12 November
item.description: The deadline for the public to comment on the Hastings Borough Council's Draft Local Plan is Thursday 12 November, and one of the most argued-over parts of it is what happens to the Convent of the Holy Child Jesus in Lower Bohemia.

item.title: Council to seek group to take lease of Hollington Community Centre
item.description: East Sussex County Council is looking for a local group to take on the lease of Hollington Community Centre in Old Church Road, after saying the building needs significant investment to bring it back into good repair.

item.title: Update: Hastings Castle to get £288,500 from Historic England for repairs
item.description: Following the £288,500 Historic England award and a £200,000 contribution from the council, the first phase of conservation works at Hastings Castle has begun, with specialist contractors removing vegetation from sections of the castle walls and the motte. The works are due to be completed by 16 November.

item.title: Hastings council to consider Age Friendly strategy for older residents
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has drawn up an Age Friendly Hastings Strategy and Action Plan, with proposals to make the town more accessible and inclusive for people aged 50 and over.

item.title: Free parking at Hastings council car parks in December
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has agreed plans to provide free parking at its council-owned car parks on specific dates in the run-up to Christmas.

item.title: One East Sussex reorganisation to proceed, with four Lewes wards moving to Brighton
item.description: The Government has announced it is minded to proceed with local government reorganisation in East Sussex, Hastings Borough Council has said.

item.title: Secondary school applications close at midnight today
item.description: Parents and carers in East Sussex have until midnight today to submit applications for secondary school places for September 2027.

item.title: Hastings Cabinet to discuss fee freeze and heritage funding on 9 November
item.description: Hastings Borough Council's Cabinet will meet on Monday 9 November to discuss a range of reports, the council said.

item.title: Update: Bexhill empty shops plan opens for public consultation
item.description: The council leader says the draft Local Plan consultation remains open until Tuesday, November 24, and the Tapestry development in Battle, which will provide 200 energy-efficient homes, has been shortlisted for the Best Development Award at the Inside Housing Development Awards.

item.title: Update: Holiday lets, flats and shops approved for arcade blaze site in George Street
item.description: Residents have divided over the approved scheme. One, writing on the Observer's Facebook page, said: "We don't need holiday lets and more shops; we need housing." Others suggested affordable bedsits or a hub for young people, while a handful backed the development.

item.title: Update: Bexhill seafront fountain replacement reaches procurement stage
item.description: More has emerged on the plans to reinstate the fountain on the front lawns of the De La Warr Pavilion in Bexhill. Rother District Council will lead the procurement process as both landowner and accountable body for the funding, and Bexhill-on-Sea Town Council has agreed in principle to take on future maintenance responsibilities, subject to lease and construction quality arrangements, The Argus reported. The project forms part of the Bexhill Neighbourhood Board's four-year Regeneration Investment Plan and is funded through the Government's Pride in Place programme.

item.title: Update: Bexhill seafront fountain replacement reaches procurement stage
item.description: Rother's Cabinet has formally agreed to use funding from the Pride in Place programme budget to replace the Bexhill seafront fountain and splashpad, the council said. Cllr Hazel Timpe described the fountain as "a much-loved community asset" whose loss had been "keenly felt".

item.title: Rother to consult on 2027/28 budget with £2.72m in reserves
item.description: Residents of Rother are set to be consulted on how the council will balance its 2027/28 budget, after Cabinet agreed on 26 October to consult staff, the public and, for the first time, individual organisations likely to be affected by savings decisions.

item.title: New road signs installed in Bexhill for horse and rider safety
item.description: New road signs have been installed in Bexhill as part of a campaign to make roads safer for horses and riders, a town councillor said.

item.title: New litter bins appear in Hastings under Pride in Place funding
item.description: New litter bins are being installed around Hastings as part of the government's Pride in Place scheme, which saw the town awarded £20 million.

item.title: Rother District Council pre-election event for would-be candidates in May 2027
item.description: Rother District Council is holding an online pre-election event for people considering standing as a councillor in May 2027.

item.title: Hastings to receive £1m from the government's derelict buildings fund
item.description: Hastings has been awarded £1 million from the government's Derelict Buildings Fund, according to the Hastings Observer.

item.title: Gorse cutting begins at Firehills in Hastings Country Park
item.description: Hastings Borough Council is to cut back the gorse that grows in the Firehills area of Hastings Country Park.

item.title: Hastings to get £1.2 million Fairness Fund for community projects
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has launched The Fairness Fund, a £1.2 million programme to support community-led projects that improve opportunities, health and wellbeing in the parts of the town where funding is needed most.

item.title: Holiday lets, flats and shops approved for arcade blaze site in George Street
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has approved plans for 20 flats, six holiday lets and four commercial units on the site of the former amusement arcade in George Street, Old Town, which was destroyed in a fire in January 2023.

item.title: Appeal for information after quad bikes stolen from Nurdle charity
item.description: Beach cleaning charity Nurdle is appealing for information after three quad bikes and specialist equipment were stolen from secure shipping containers in the early hours of Sunday 25 October.

item.title: Bexhill seafront fountain replacement reaches procurement stage
item.description: A fountain is to return to the front lawns of the De La Warr Pavilion, with the replacement project now at the procurement stage.

item.title: White Rock Gardens could get covered padel and tennis courts
item.description: Hastings Borough Council says it is being considered to receive £1.3million from the Lawn Tennis Association to develop a covered tennis and padel centre at White Rock Gardens.

item.title: Leaders of three councils urge government to raise Local Housing Allowance
item.description: Councillors in Hastings, Lewes and Eastbourne have asked the government to raise the housing benefit rates that help people pay private rents.

item.title: Plans to reopen Marina Pavilion in St Leonards held up in dispute with council
item.description: The reopening of the Marina Pavilion on the St Leonards seafront has been delayed amid a row over council repair demands.

item.title: Storm power cuts threatened water supply to the Hastings area
item.description: Two water supply works serving the Hastings area shut down over the weekend after the storms knocked out local power, though taps kept running.

item.title: Fears of hungry children over half-term after holiday food vouchers axed
item.description: Families across East Sussex have not received automatic food vouchers for the October half term after the county council ended the school holiday scheme, raising fears that vulnerable children could go hungry.

item.title: Hastings Castle to get £288,500 from Historic England for repairs
item.description: Hastings Borough Council has been awarded £288,500 from Historic England's Heritage at Risk Capital Fund for repairs to Hastings Castle.

item.title: Bexhill empty shops plan opens for public consultation
item.description: Rother District Council has asked residents and businesses to have their say on a plan to tackle long-term empty shops in Bexhill.

item.title: West Hill Lift gets £531,000 from National Lottery Heritage Fund
item.description: The National Lottery Heritage Fund has offered £531,000 in development funding to Hastings Borough Council to secure the long-term future of the West Hill Lift, the Grade II listed lift that runs up the cliff from George Street to Hastings Castle.
